gate.deploySummary: The SC-3423 fix is clean and safe to deploy. I verified the three deploy files (HardwareGroupController.cls, hardwareGroupManager.js, HardwareGroupControllerTest.cls) by retrieving the LIVE FortraUAT versions and diffing: the deploy is an exact superset of the live state, adding only the new getHardwareById(Id) @AuraEnabled (non-cacheable) method, the ORDER BY Hardware_ID__c NULLS LAST / LIMIT 200->2000 edits on searchHardware and getUnassignedHardware, the LWC swap of searchHardware(...).find() for an O(1) getHardwareById read-after-write, the now-conditional success toast (moved inside if(createdHardware) with an honest Warning + form-kept-open else branch), and two test methods. No compile risk: all 11 fields selected by getHardwareById exist on Hardware__c, the LWC named param {hardwareId} matches the Apex signature, searchHardware remains imported and used (handleSearchHardware), and no stale .find()/newHardwareRecords remain. No regression: the HTML template is byte-identical to live, no other methods or call sites are touched, the Create Group button un-greys correctly via canFinish -> selectedHardware !== null, and the largest real account (1172 Hardware rows) sits well under LIMIT 2000 with no governor concern. The bug is genuinely fixed on both axes: the new record is now retrieved deterministically by Id (immune to the 200-row/NULLS-FIRST window that dropped it), and the previously unconditional success toast is now gated so a failed selection surfaces a Warning instead of a false success. The deploy test will execute: there are no Apex triggers on Hardware__c and all three active validation rules pass for the 205-row seed and the created record (formulas inspected; Pending/Cross Platform/Quoting confirmed valid picklist values). The only caveats are non-blocking test-strength and list-cap follow-ups noted below.

The fix is correct, but the test does not actually lock the regression closed.
